## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Mark two holes on each end of the light bar underside and a central hole for wires using a Sharpie.
2. [Partial] Drill out those marked holes to match the size of four zip ties.
3. [Partial] Clean the drilled areas on the hood to prevent rust buildup.
4. [Partial] Apply touch-up paint over the cleaned spots.
5. [Partial] Insert the four zip ties through the newly painted and dried holes in the hood structure.
6. Feed the light wires into the outer holes where the zip ties are positioned.
7. Secure the lights with included 3M tape and tighten the zip ties to lock them in place.
8. Route the positive wire down along the passenger side of the hood structure.
9. Run the ground wire down along the driver's side of the hood structure.
10. Extend one power lead across the front of the hood from its respective side.
11. Connect a corresponding ground wire across the front of the hood to meet the other side.
12. Solder all connections together, tying hots and grounds into bundles.
13. Unplug the hood sensor connector to isolate it for testing.
14. Use a multimeter or continuity tester to identify which wire in the plug goes directly to ground by probing against an engine bay ground point.
15. Identify the remaining wire as the active signal needed to complete the circuit when the hood opens.
16. Tie that identified sensor wire to the main light ground using a tap splice.
17. Connect the hot power lead from the lights directly to the battery, skipping a fuse for simplicity.
18. Plug the previously removed hood sensor back into its connector securely.
19. Test all electrical connections to ensure proper function.
20. [Partial] Shrink heat wrap over every soldered and spliced connection point.
21. [Partial] Tuck any excess wire length up inside the hood structure.

_Procedure reported by [t1497]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-under-hood-lights-done-easy-and-cheap.7292/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1220] [Partial]</summary>

1. Purchase two 450-strand fiber optic units (approx. 13 feet long) to cover the roof area.
2. Acquire a used headliner from a junkyard as a backup in case of failure.
3. [Partial] Have the new headliner reupholstered if necessary before starting installation.
4. Divide the headliner surface into eight distinct sections for even distribution.
5. Plot and drill holes across all nine hundred locations, placing 112 strands per section plus four extras.
6. [Partial] Split each main fiber optic bundle into eight sets of 112 strands to feed every grid equally.
7. [Partial] Feed the individual strands through their respective drilled holes one by one (a time-consuming process).
8. Secure all nine hundred strands in place using hot glue on day five.
9. [Partial] Trim the excess strand length slightly so they fit easily without being too long, leaving some slack for adjustments later.
10. Remove and replace the original headliner with the new fiber-optic integrated version.
11. Splice into the front 12-volt outlet power wire to utilize ACC mode operation.
12. Run a wire from the splice location toward the rear under the seats and carpet to hide it.
13. Connect the run wire to two female 12-volt outlets purchased separately for distribution.
14. [Partial] Hide all wiring connections behind interior trim panels so they are invisible when off.
15. Mount the main fiber optic units behind the wheel wells, positioned near the rear cubbies.

</details>

## Tips & gotchas

- Use gloves when removing the hot headlight from the oven for dexterity and heat protection. [t1851]
- Lay a piece of aluminum foil across the bottom grate in the gas oven to deflect direct heat. [t1851]
- [Partial] Use a long skinny flat-head screwdriver specifically for reaching the clips. [t1851]
- Pull each clip one at a time until the squares line up before popping it off. [t1851]
- Tilt the headlight down toward the ground after removing bolts to pop loose the inside lower corner. [t1851]
- [Partial] Note that one bolt is on top of the fender and the other is in the upper inside corner. [t1851]
- The factory parking/turn signal harness must be physically moved or adapted for the projector setup. [t1851]
- Mount the relay box high up, ideally where the factory battery sits. [t1851]
- Secure one end with a single self-tapping screw and zip-tie the other. [t1851]
- If these specific wires aren't reversed, the high beam and low beam functions will swap. [t1851]
- This step is necessary because of how the relay harness interfaces with the stock plug. [t1851]
- Use self-tapping screws with 3/8" diameter nylon spacers (3/4" long) for mounting. [t1851]
- [Partial] Seal the input plug from the relay harness where it connects to the ballast, as this is a weak point. [t1851]
- [Partial] Fill any unused plugs with sealant if only one connector is used by the relay. [t1851]
- Verify polarity on LED markers before final attachment to avoid rework. [t1851]
- Align the headlights according to manufacturer specifications (e.g., TRS website) once mounted. [t1851]
- [Partial] Perform final aiming in low-light conditions. [t1851]
- Consider using a DDM Tuning HID kit for bulbs and ballasts to reduce parts cost. [t1851]
- Position the light bar so it shines directly at the engine rather than in your face when opening the hood. [t1497]
- [Partial] Ensure one ground exists on one side and power leads up the other before crossing them across the front of the hood. [t1497]
- Ground the negative side of the system. [t2226]
- [Partial] Use a fuse in-line with the red power wire. [t2226]
- [Partial] This method keeps the radio on only when the key is turned to run position. [t2226]
- Route the wire down under the glove box and dash area. [t2226]
- Run wires behind the center console to reach the cab. [t2226]
- Ensure the mount is waterproofed to protect against side exposure. [t2226]
- [Partial] Consider using a longer antenna (approx 5') if mounting on the flat rear section. [t2226]
- [Partial] Screw the ground bolt directly into steel for best contact. [t2226]
- A good ground is essential to prevent signal loss. [t2226]
- [Partial] Decide if insulation is needed where the connector meets grounded metal roof surfaces. [t2226]
- This setup allows unthreading the cable from inside the truck to remove the unit. [t2226]
- Note that this setup may require resetting CB channels every time the car is turned off. [t2226]
- Ensure the antenna is free of obstructions, including people holding an SWR meter if hooked up to the antenna side. [t2327]
- A semi-empty parking lot provides decent tuning conditions even without a wide-open field. [t2327]
- Plotting and drilling holes in sections helps prevent losing count. [t1220]
- Feeding strands into manageable chunks makes the tedious process easier. [t1220]
- Leaving strands slightly untrimmed allows for re-pulling if they get snagged during installation. [t1220]
- The system cycles through 7 colors at different speeds with a twinkle effect. [t1220]
- Use the entire roof surface to act as a ground plane for even radiation distribution. [t2332]
- [Partial] If mounting toward the back, most energy will transmit rearward; centering it gives better overall range. [t2332]
- Ground the antenna itself in addition to grounding the vehicle's ground plane. [t2332]
- Use a hot wire and ground from the selected circuit. [t2332]
- Place a plate under the lights running up to the glass to minimize light reflection on the windshield. [t2333]
- [Partial] Ground the lights directly to the vehicle frame rather than relying on switch grounds. [t1609]
- [Partial] Use an 8-gauge wire for power and ground running from the battery block to the body/frame, then use smaller gauge wiring (e.g., 12-14) for distribution. [t1609]
- Use a contained unit to simplify multiple relays and fuses. [t1609]
- [Partial] Install the 6-way switch on top of the dashboard or center console. [t1609]

## Common mistakes

- Painting the reflector before drilling out the hole, requiring paint removal afterward. [t1851]
- Using a step drill that is too small for the projector stem without enlarging it first. [t1851]
- [Partial] Mounting the antenna on the passenger side if a kayak rack is present. [t2097]
- [Partial] Not trimming fibers evenly, resulting in noticeable spots where something looks off when the lights are off. [t1220]
- [Partial] Leaving loose fabric from the reupholstered headliner visible after installation. [t1220]
- [Partial] Mounting too far back where the roof line cuts off the majority of the antenna length. [t2332]
- [Partial] Light reflecting back into driver's eyes at night due to interior placement. [t2333]
- [Partial] Terrible flashback on the dashboard because all lights illuminate too fast in constant patterns. [t2333]
- [Partial] Overheating or potential electrical fires if switches are not rated correctly for voltage/amp load. [t1609]
- [Partial] Having too many individual power leads running to the battery, making future mods difficult. [t1609]
